name: prev_day_hl_breakout_v1
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: When NIFTY closes above its previous day high (PDH) for three consecutive 5-second bars, overnight short-sellers' stop orders clustered just above PDH have been swept, removing the supply ceiling and creating a micro-liquidity vacuum. Simultaneously, breakout-scanning algorithms (dozens of which monitor PDH/PDL on NIFTY in real time) detect the confirmed level breach and inject fresh buy orders, accelerating the index 15-30 spot points beyond PDH within 30-90 seconds before the first wave of mean-reversion algos absorbs momentum. The symmetric logic applies at PDL for bearish breaks: trapped longs exit, shorts pile in, and the first 15-25 spot point decline is the most momentum-rich phase. PDH/PDL on NIFTY carries more weight than on individual stocks because every market participant — retail, institutional, FII — uses the same reference level for the same index.

indicators.name: pdh
indicators.purpose: Previous day's absolute high. No lookback — this is a fixed session-level constant that resets each trading day. Used as the supply ceiling whose breach signals stop-cluster sweep.

indicators.name: pdl
indicators.purpose: Previous day's absolute low. Symmetric to PDH. No lookback scaling required — it is a daily anchor, not a rolling indicator.

indicators.name: vwap
indicators.formula: cumsum(typical_price * volume) / cumsum(volume) from session open per day
indicators.purpose: Session VWAP from 09:15 each day. Cumulative measure — no scaling needed. Used as directional filter: a PDH breakout with price ABOVE VWAP confirms institutional demand is net positive for the day; a PDL break with price BELOW VWAP confirms net selling pressure. Prevents trading counter-trend to the dominant intraday flow.

indicators.name: rel_vol_240
indicators.purpose: Current 5-second bar volume relative to its 20-minute (240-bar) rolling average. The original used SMA(20) on 1-minute bars — the same 20-minute baseline, preserved exactly because the relative volume threshold is about identifying above-average participation at the breakout moment, and a 20-minute reference window provides a stable intraday baseline. A reading > 1.5x confirms genuine order flow at the level, not a passive drift through PDH/PDL on thin volume.

indicators.name: consec_3
indicators.formula: close > pdh for bars [i-2, i-1, i]
indicators.purpose: 3-bar (15-second) persistence filter to reject single-wick spikes through PDH/PDL. Original used 3 x 1-minute bars (3-minute confirmation) to filter fakes — compressed to 15 seconds because at 5s resolution a genuine breakout holds above the level immediately while spike-and-reverse behavior typically resolves within 1-2 bars. We cannot wait 3 minutes (36 bars) as that misses the entire first move.

conditions: vix_close < vix_max (default 24, avoid extreme fear regimes)
buy_ce.confirmation: All 4 conditions simultaneously true on the same bar

buy_pe.confirmation: All 4 conditions simultaneously true on the same bar

exit.stop_rationale: 4 option points ≈ 8 spot points at delta 0.5. A confirmed PDH break on NIFTY that reverses 8+ spot points back inside PDH within 90 seconds is a proven false breakout (stop-hunt). At that retracement depth the supply ceiling has reasserted and the continuation thesis is invalidated. Calibrated to the 15-second NIFTY typical move of 1-3 pts — stop is wider than noise but tighter than a full reversal.
exit.target_rationale: 7 option points ≈ 14 spot points at delta 0.5. First continuation leg after genuine PDH break on NIFTY covers 15-30 spot points within 30-90 seconds (1-min move range: 3-7 pts option; 2-min: 5-10 pts). Target of 7 pts captures the median of the 30-90 second expected move and delivers 1.75:1 reward-to-risk ratio.

filters.vix_filter: vix < 24 — above 24 NIFTY becomes too volatile for stop-level precision; PDH/PDL becomes less predictive as range expansion dominates
filters.time_filter: 09:20-15:20 IST — skip first 5 minutes of chaotic price discovery; stop at 15:20 to avoid EOD illiquidity
filters.volume_filter: rel_vol_240 > 1.5 — breakout must have above-average volume participation to distinguish from passive drift
filters.trend_filter: close vs VWAP — long side only when price above VWAP, short side only when below

edge.edge_decay_risk: medium — PDH/PDL is widely watched and the setup is crowded; edge comes from speed (enter within 15 seconds) and volume confirmation filtering out false breaks

adaptation_notes: Key changes from original equity strategy: (1) Universe changed from NIFTY100 stocks to NIFTY index — single liquid instrument vs portfolio; (2) 3-bar confirmation compressed from 3 x 1-min (3 min) to 3 x 5-sec (15 sec) — at 5s resolution we need early entry to capture the initial move impulse; (3) Relative volume lookback kept at 20-minute baseline (240 bars at 5s = same calendar time as original 20 x 1-min); (4) ATR-based targets replaced with fixed option premium points calibrated to 30-90s NIFTY move magnitudes; (5) VWAP filter retained as directional context; (6) Trailing stop removed — too complex for 15-90s holds; (7) Session narrowed to 09:20-15:20 to avoid pre-open noise and EOD illiquidity.
weaknesses: PDH/PDL is widely known — stop-hunting algos deliberately push NIFTY through these levels and reverse, creating false breakout patterns. The 3-bar filter and volume requirement reduce but do not eliminate this risk.
On days when NIFTY opens above PDH (gap-up), the breakout level is never tested intraday and no signals fire.

PDH/PDL levels on NIFTY are exactly as wide as the prior day's range — on high-volatility days the level is far from current price and rarely reached; on low-volatility days it is reached frequently with weak follow-through.
The volume filter (rel_vol > 1.5) at 5-second bars is noisy — a single large block trade can trigger the filter on a single bar without representing genuine broad participation.

_source.original_stop: 0.3% from entry or back inside PDH/PDL
